findings.title: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but is invoked by the client-removal event listener
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) when a ClientRemovedEvent fires and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. Since MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, removing any client while V2 is active will crash the event handler with an unhandled exception, likely aborting the client deletion. The method should be a no-op (or the event listener should skip V2-incompatible operations) instead of throwing.

findings.title: canView() does not account for MANAGE permission, breaking manage-implies-view invariant
findings.body: canView() only checks canViewClientDefault() (role-based) and hasPermission(VIEW). It does not check hasPermission(MANAGE). A user granted a global MANAGE permission on all clients will have canManage() return true but canView() return false, which is inconsistent: manage should imply view. This can cause the user to be unable to list clients even though they can manage them. The method should also return true when hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) is true.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the new CLIENTS resource type
findings.body: getResourceName handles USERS by resolving the user and returning the username, but has no branch for CLIENTS. When a policy's resourceType is "Clients", the method falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). For individual client resources the name is the internal client ID (set by resolveClient), and getDisplayName() is likely null or unhelpful. A branch analogous to USERS should resolve the ClientModel and return client.getClientId(), and return "All clients" for the type-level resource.

findings.title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext method is defined but never called
findings.body: The private method getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) at line 262 is never invoked anywhere in the class. It also references the unused static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46). This dead code adds confusion about the intended design and should be removed or wired in if it is needed for canExchangeTo support in the future.

findings.title: canMapRoles does not fall back to admin role check, unlike canManage and canConfigure
findings.body: canMapRoles(ClientModel) only calls hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES). Unlike canManage(ClientModel) which first checks root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS), canMapRoles does not check any admin role. In V1, having MANAGE_CLIENTS role allowed mapping roles. If the intent in V2 is that MANAGE_CLIENTS role should still grant MAP_ROLES capability (as the interface Javadoc implies by referencing the V1 scope), the admin role check is missing. If it is intentionally excluded, the interface Javadoc should be updated to clarify.
